pageCache.pageTitle: Inclusion and SEND | Chesham Bois Church of England Combined School
pageCache.text:
Inclusion and SEND
CBS SEN Vision Statement
Christian values are at the heart of everything we do at Chesham Bois CE School. Inclusion, and valuing the diversity and richness of our community, is central to our daily practice. Every child, regardless of their needs, faith, ability, gender, ethnicity, background or circumstances, is valued, nurtured and supported to become an independent learner who fulfils their potential.
We are committed to ensuring that every child experiences the journey of a CBS child. Individual strengths, talents and achievements are celebrated and valued by all members of our school community.
We are dedicated to ensuring that appropriate provision is in place for all children with additional needs. By removing barriers to learning and creating equitable access to opportunities, we enable every child to reach their full potential and to be well prepared for the next stage of their education. We believe that children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) can thrive and be the very best they can be both academically and socially and emotionally; developing self-belief, positive wellbeing alongside academic success.
Providing an inclusive, high-quality universal offer built on strong collaboration and effective information sharing.
Delivering a challenging curriculum with high expectations and ambition for all learners.
Placing the child, their interests and their individual strengths at the centre of their learning journey.
Embedding nurture, positive relationships and our CARE culture throughout school life.
Working in close partnership with parents and carers.
Maintaining a "keep pace with peers" approach rather than a "catch up with peers" model through targeted pre- and post-teaching interventions, while also using technology to support adaptive teaching and increase access to learning.
We have carefully considered our physical and learning environments to ensure they are as inclusive, accessible and responsive as possible to the diverse needs of all learners in our context. Through thoughtful classroom design, consistency across the school, visual supports, adaptive resources and predictable routines and language, we aim to create spaces where children feel safe, supported and able to thrive.
SENDCo - Mrs K. Hassan
Assistant SENCO - Mrs S. Harwood
Inclusion Manager - Mrs C. Groves
Inclusion Governor - Mrs K. Wilson

pageCache.pageTitle: Open Morning | Chesham Bois Church of England Combined School
pageCache.text:
Open Morning
Chesham Bois CE School warmly welcomes prospective parents for our September 2027 intake to visit our vibrant and happy school.
Tours with our Year 6 children with an opportunity to ask further questions will be available on the following dates:
Thursday 1st October 9:45am presentation and tour 10:45am presentation and tour
Thursday 15th October 9:45am presentation and tour 10:45am presentation and tour
Thursday 12th November 9:45am presentation and tour 10:45am presentation and tour
Please note spaces are limited on each tour so booking is essential. Tours can be booked by contacting the school office via email office@cbs.odbst.org or 01494 726901
We look forward to seeing you soon.
Frequently Asked Questions
1. We don't live in your catchment area; are we likely to get a place?
Our catchment area would never fill a class; we take 30 children in EYFS and most years the majority of the class are children who live outside of our catchment area.
In 2025 - 2026 intake:
5 children in our catchment area
6 children are siblings
19 children non-catchment area (decided by distance from the school)
2. Does the school offer breakfast and after school care?
Unfortunately, we do not have the facilities to provide wrap around care. However, Twirlies and Twilight (run separately from the school) do offer breakfast club and after school provision. These childcare providers run from the Scout Hut which is next to the school and will walk the children to school in the morning and will collect them from school at 3:15pm. Twirlies operates between 7:30 and 8:30am. Twilight operates between 3:15pm and 5:30pm.
3. What time can I drop my child at school?
The school gate opens at 8:30am and the children go straight to their classrooms to start early morning work. Registration is at 8:45am.
4. What are assemblies like at the school?
We have an assembly everyday. On a Monday the Headteacher leads assembly and this is linked to either our value or focus for the half term, a story from the Bible, a religious festival or a world event. Tuesday's assemblies are lead by the children in the form of class assemblies where classes take it in turns to share their learning with the rest of the school (parents are invited to attend these). On Wednesdays a team from local churches deliver assemblies called 'Open The Bible' where stories from the Bible are acted out and explored with the children. Thursday's assemblies are our singing assemblies, lead by Miss Mitterhuber, to support the children in learning hymns and songs and developing their singing abilities. We end the week with our Celebration assemblies; these involve celebrating our Stars of the Week and the achievements of our children in and out of school.
Each assembly ends with a quiet moment of reflection and an act of collective worship; all children are invited to participate in this.
5. Which feeder schools do your child tend to go on to?
The majority of our children go to:
Chiltern Hills Academy
Dr Challoners' Grammar
6. What do the children have for lunch?
Currently our hot school meal are provided by Chartwells. All children in EYFS and KS1 are entitled to free school meals. There is a good variety of dishes on offer and there is always a meat, vegetarian and jacket potato option. Parents choose these weekly online.
7. What languages do you teach?
We teach French from the start of KS2. The school also offers a paid lunchtime French club called La Jollie Ronde.
8. Can my child learn to play a musical instrument?
From KS2, children can learn to play guitar, piano and a variety of brass and woodwind instruments. Lessons can be either in groups or individual and are paid for by parents.
Why not follow our EYFS Instagram account to see the fantastic learning opportunities our children have access to...
@littlelearnersineyfs

Preparing Children for Modern British Life
Chesham Bois CE School
Preparing Children for Modern British Life
The Department for Education states that there is a need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”.
The Department for Education defines British Values as follows:
As a Church of England School, we place the child at the centre of all we do. We welcome children and families of all faiths and of none. Our work is motivated and inspired by our core Christian values which are lived out on a daily basis by children and adults in the school. We provide a caring, nurturing learning environment in which all children can achieve and grow together.
We aim to prepare children for life in modern Britain. As such we ensure that the fundamental British values are introduced, along with our core Christian values, discussed and lived out through the ethos and work of the school.
Our Curriculum areas provide a vehicle for furthering understanding of these concepts and our collective activities such as assemblies, experiences beyond their local community, sporting events, residentials, a range of visits and visitors and special themed weeks provide excellent opportunities to deepen and develop understanding.
At Chesham Bois CE Combined School, we recognise that such development is most successful when those values and attitudes are promoted by all staff and adults and we strive to share and model behaviours for our children.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of Those with Different Faiths and Beliefs

ODBST Earrings & Jewellery Policy statement
Purpose of the Policy Statement
The Oxford Diocesan Bucks Schools Trust (ODBST) is committed to ensure that all pupils participate in in PE in a safe environment. This trust‑wide policy sets out clear expectations regarding the wearing of earrings and jewellery in order to reduce avoidable risks, in accordance with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and Association of Physical Education (afPE) guidance.
General Rules for Jewellery across ODBST Schools
- Pupils may wear one pair of small, plain stud earrings during the school day, however the school discourages the wearing of jewellery, at all times, for health and safety reasons.
- Dangly earrings, hoops, necklaces, bracelets, rings, and smart watches are not permitted.
- Staff must not insert, remove, tape, or adjust earrings for pupils.
Guidance information:
Earrings and Jewellery during PE and Physical Activity
All earrings and jewellery must be removed for PE, school sports, active play, and physical extra-curricular activities. Pupils unable to remove earrings cannot participate in practical PE. Safe keeping of removed items is the responsibility of the child.
New piercings require approximately six weeks before earrings can be safely removed. During this period, pupils who cannot remove earrings will complete non‑practical PE activities.
Taping earrings is not permitted.
The British Association of Advisers and Lecturers in PE (BAALPE) guidance supports afPE and states that earrings must be removed and must not be taped, as taping “creates a perception of safety and is not recommended.” The wearing of jewellery increases the risk of injury significantly.
Religious and Cultural Jewellery
Health and Safety law takes precedence where risk exists. Pupils do not have an unlimited right to wear religious items during activities presenting a safety risk.
Parents must ensure children can remove their earrings for PE if they wear them to school. School staff will not be able to remove pupil earrings or jewellery.
